conversations.title: I was born with cerebral palsy. Why is disability now a badge of pride for so many young people?
conversations.reply: It's amazing to see young people embracing their disabilities with such confidence, and I hope this shift in attitude leads to real change in accessibility and inclusivity.

conversations.title: Interabled Love: The Couples Defying The Odds
conversations.reply: These couples are showing the world what love is all about, and it's wonderful to see their stories being shared.

conversations.title: The intimacy question everyone is afraid to ask
conversations.reply: It's time we started talking openly about intimacy and disability, and breaking down the stigma that surrounds it.

conversations.title: We just want to be treated equally’ Wheelchair users hit out over OMD concert access
conversations.reply: It's shocking that wheelchair users are still facing barriers like this, and I hope the venue takes steps to make sure everyone can access their events.

conversations.title: Accessibility map hailed a success at Brightlingsea event
conversations.reply: This is exactly the kind of initiative that can make a real difference, and I'm so glad to see it's been a success.

conversations.title: Euan's Guide helps disabled people find accessible places with confidence
conversations.reply: Euan's Guide is doing fantastic work, and it's great to see people feeling more confident about accessing new places.

conversations.title: DD40 - Mikel Erentxun - Duncan Dhu Tour 2026 at The Clapham Grand, London
conversations.reply: I hope The Clapham Grand takes note of the need for better accessibility, so everyone can enjoy their events.

conversations.title: New Zealand Artist Rebecca Bond Discusses 'Drawing on Disability' Festival and Accessible Art
conversations.reply: Rebecca Bond's work is a great example of how art can be made more accessible and inclusive, and I love seeing this kind of innovation.

mission:
Task: today's Able2Love engagement round (2026-08-10). You are working in my logged-in browser as the app's accounts: @Able2LoveApp on X, @able2loveapp on Instagram.

APPROVAL RULE, NEVER BREAK IT: before posting anything, show me the post you found and your drafted reply, and wait for my yes. Never post without a yes for that specific item. If I say no or skip, find a replacement candidate so we still hit today's targets.

TARGETS: 10 replies on X and 5 comments on Instagram, found and posted a few at a time (pause whenever I say pause). Skip and tell me if we run out of genuinely good candidates; never pad with weak ones.

FINDING CANDIDATES:
- X: use x.com search (Latest tab) for: disability dating, dating with a disability, accessible venue, wheelchair nightlife, #DisabilityDating, #DisabledAndDating, chronic illness dating, plus anything matching today's ammo below. Real people only: skip news outlets, brands, giveaways, and anything about death, grief, tragedy or self-harm.
- Instagram: work through the hit-list below (hashtag pages and creator types), picking recent posts where a comment genuinely fits.

VOICE, NON-NEGOTIABLE: write from the Able2Love account like a real person who built it and cares, warm and on the poster's side. React to what each post actually is: agree and back people up when they've had a rough time, help when they ask, be glad for them when they celebrate. You HAVE an opinion, warm agreement not cold analysis, all tracing back to one belief: the way disabled daters get treated on the big apps is wrong and this app is changing it. Usually 1 to 2 short sentences on X, shorter is fine for IG. UK English. NEVER use an em dash or en dash. Disability is never the punchline. Never invent facts, studies, numbers, or claims about any venue, person, company, or the app's features. Never argue; skip hostile threads. Never preachy or lecturing: no "access should be the baseline", "legal requirement", "not a favour", "stark reminder", "raising awareness", "it's time to". Never negative at the person. Every reply a different shape: never reuse a phrase across replies, never post the ammo lines verbatim.

TODAY'S AMMO (adapt these angles to the actual post in front of you, reworded fresh every time):
- It's amazing to see young people embracing their disabilities with such confidence, and I hope this shift in attitude leads to real change in accessibility and inclusivity.

- Euan's Guide is doing fantastic work, and it's great to see people feeling more confident about accessing new places.
- I hope The Clapham Grand takes note of the need for better accessibility, so everyone can enjoy their events.
- Rebecca Bond's work is a great example of how art can be made more accessible and inclusive, and I love seeing this kind of innovation.
